newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk public sector unions reach wage agreement.
newsitem.headline: Turk public sector unions reach wage agreement.

text.p: Turkish State Minister Nevzat Ercan said an agreement had been reached with public sector workers belonging to the labour confederation Turk-Is, Anatolian news agency said on Sunday.

Ercan said a deal was done with five major unions representing less than one third of the 500,000-strong Turk-Is membership and he expected the other unions in the confederation also to sign up to the agreement.
"I want this excellent agreement which has been reached and the peaceful environment which has been provided to be eternal in Turkish working life," the agency quoted Ercan as saying.

Under the agreement, 142,000 workers from the electrical, water, gas, paper, farm, forestry, health and news sectors will receive a 38 percent pay rise, less than the annual inflation rate of just over 80 percent.

In addition, the deal gives them a payment of eight million Turkish lira for the first six months of the year, an extra 1.4 million lira for those with wages below 30 million lira, plus payments for seniority, the agency said.
Pay increments were to be linked to inflation and paid every six months, Ercan said.
Turk-Is members had stepped up industrial action on Thursday, with 22,000 workers at state oil and petrochemical plants blocking shipments and 34,000 arms workers holding marches.
